correctness.rationale: Let A=a+B with 0 in B, H=<B> finite; kB are strictly increasing until H, since equality kB=(k+1)B forces invariance under all of H. Earliest full stage is exactly index mu, while eventual cosets ka+H have period ord(a+H)=lambda. For mu>=2 cardinalities require |H|>=|B|+mu-1>=mu+1 and lambda divides [G:H], giving sharp order. Equality forces |B|=2 and subgroup H generated by its difference b with order mu+1; quotient generated by a+H. Explicit G=C_{(mu+1)lambda}, A={1,1+lambda} reaches bound, and C_lambda singleton realizes mu=1, including lambda=1. Independent cyclic-group subset enumeration through group order 10 checked 2036 nonempty subsets including 162 extremal cases. Universal proof is the strict-chain argument, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Least finite group order is a natural resource invariant for representations of every finite cyclic semigroup. The exact all-pair optimal formula and complete characterization of minimizers, including existence of cyclic optimal hosts, constitute a meaningful natural classification beyond mere embeddability.

final_claim: For positive index mu and period lambda of finite monogenic semigroup S_{mu,lambda}, the least size of a finite abelian group G with an embedding in its nonempty-subset power semigroup is lambda for mu=1 and (mu+1)*lambda for mu>=2. Every order-minimal generator subset is a singleton (mu=1) or A={a,a+b} with ord(b)=mu+1, H=<b>, and a+H generator of the cyclic quotient G/H of order lambda; a cyclic host realizes each optimum.
limitations: Finite abelian groups, nonempty subsets and monogenic target semigroups only.
Finite enumeration for group orders <=10 corroborates but does not prove the universal theorem.
2025 and 1980 plausible priority risks remain uninspected; no absolute novelty guarantee.
